passages.title: 阿里山林鐵終於全線通車
passages.text: The Alishan Forest Railway in Chiayi is more than 100 years old. It was first built in 1912 to carry wood down the mountain. In 2009, Typhoon Morakot damaged the railway in more than 400 places, so the {1} could not go all the way up to Alishan. For about 15 years, most visitors had to {2} in cars or buses to get to the top. After many years of hard work, the whole line opened again in July 2024. Now four trains run every day between Chiayi and Alishan, and the trip is about 71 kilometers long. There are also two new tourist trains. Last month, my family went to Alishan. We took the {3} up the mountain and saw clouds below us. It was much more fun than {4} in a car! My little brother said the train was like a slow {5} flying above the sea of clouds.

blanks.why: the train could not go all the way up「火車沒辦法一路開上山」。spoon（湯匙）、pumpkin（南瓜）、towel（毛巾）都不會在鐵路上行駛。
ride in cars or buses「搭汽車或公車」，ride in + 交通工具。fry（炸）、boil（煮）、iron（燙）都不能接 in cars 表示搭乘。
took the train up the mountain「搭火車上山」，take the train 是搭火車。blanket（毯子）、lemon（檸檬）、sofa（沙發）都不能搭乘。
more fun than riding in a car「比坐車有趣」，than 後面用動名詞 riding。frying、ironing、mopping 都不能接 in a car 表示乘車。
like a slow plane flying above the sea of clouds「像一架在雲海上飛的慢速飛機」。soup（湯）、cough（咳嗽）、candle（蠟燭）都不會飛。

passages.zh: 嘉義的阿里山林業鐵路已經有一百多年的歷史，最早在 1912 年建造，用來把木材運下山。2009 年，莫拉克颱風讓鐵路有四百多處受損，火車沒辦法一路開到阿里山。大約十五年來，大部分遊客只能搭汽車或公車上山頂。經過多年的努力，全線在 2024 年 7 月重新通車。現在每天有四班火車往返嘉義和阿里山，全程大約 71 公里，還有兩列新的觀光列車。上個月，我們全家去了阿里山。我們搭火車上山，看到雲在我們下面。這比坐車有趣多了！我弟弟說，這列火車就像一架在雲海上慢慢飛的飛機。

passages.title: 世界最大的郵輪
passages.text: In January 2024, the world's largest cruise {1}, Icon of the Seas, started its first trip from Miami in the United States. It is about 365 meters long, longer than three soccer fields. It has 20 decks, seven swimming pools, and six water slides. It can carry up to 7,600 passengers, and about 2,350 workers take care of them. Before the trip, soccer star Lionel Messi and his Inter Miami teammates helped {2} the ship in a special ceremony. My aunt went on a cruise last year. To get to the port, she took a {3} to Miami first. On the ship, she could {4} the water slides, watch shows, and eat at many restaurants. She said the ship was like a floating city. "It was so big that I got lost twice," she laughed. "I needed a map more than I do at a {5} station!"

blanks.why: the world's largest cruise ship「世界最大的郵輪」，cruise ship 是郵輪。spoon（湯匙）、sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）都不能載客出航。
helped welcome the ship「幫忙迎接這艘船」，help + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 the ship 用在典禮上。
took a plane to Miami「搭飛機到邁阿密」。towel（毛巾）、candle（蠟燭）、pumpkin（南瓜）都不能搭乘。
ride the water slides「玩滑水道」，ride 也可以用在遊樂設施。fry、iron、mop 都不能接 water slides。
a train station「火車站」，比喻地方大到需要地圖。cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）、drawer（抽屜）都不能和 station 組成地點。

passages.zh: 2024 年 1 月，世界最大的郵輪「海洋標誌號」從美國邁阿密展開第一趟航程。它長約 365 公尺，比三個足球場還長，有 20 層甲板、七座游泳池和六條滑水道，最多可以載 7,600 名乘客，還有大約 2,350 名工作人員照顧他們。出航前，足球明星梅西和他在國際邁阿密隊的隊友在一場特別的典禮上幫忙迎接這艘船。我阿姨去年去搭過郵輪。為了到港口，她先搭飛機到邁阿密。在船上，她可以玩滑水道、看表演，還能在很多餐廳吃飯。她說這艘船就像一座漂浮的城市。「船大到我迷路了兩次，」她笑著說，「我比在火車站還需要地圖！」

passages.title: 被「筷子」接住的火箭
passages.text: Starship, made by the company SpaceX, is the biggest rocket ever built. It has two parts: a huge booster at the bottom and a {1} on top. Most rockets are used only once, but SpaceX wants to use Starship again and again, like an airplane. On October 13, 2024, the booster flew back to its launch tower in Texas after about seven minutes. Two giant metal arms on the tower, called "chopsticks," caught it in the air! Meanwhile, the top part flew halfway around the world and came down in the Indian Ocean as planned. Our science teacher showed us the video. She said that one day, people might {2} rockets the way we take a {3} today. My friend joked that he would rather take a {4} to school, because chopsticks are only for noodles. Still, everyone in class {5} when the booster was caught.

blanks.why: a ship on top「上面的太空船」，Starship 的上半節就叫 ship。spoon、sock、cookie 都不能放在火箭上面飛行。
people might ride rockets「人們可能會搭火箭」，might + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 rockets 表示搭乘。
the way we take a plane today「就像我們現在搭飛機一樣」。pumpkin、towel、lemon 都不能搭乘。
take a train to school「搭火車上學」。blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）、wallet（錢包）都不是交通工具。
everyone cheered「大家都歡呼」。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能描寫人看到好消息的反應。

gloss: 美國太空探索科技公司
passages.zh: 由 SpaceX 公司打造的「星艦」是史上最大的火箭，它分成兩部分：底部巨大的推進器，以及上方的太空船。大部分的火箭只能用一次，但 SpaceX 希望星艦能像飛機一樣一用再用。2024 年 10 月 13 日，推進器在飛行大約七分鐘後飛回德州的發射塔，塔上兩支被稱為「筷子」的巨大金屬手臂在空中把它接住了！同時，上半部則繞了地球大半圈，照計畫降落在印度洋。我們的自然老師給我們看這段影片。她說有一天，人們可能會像現在搭飛機一樣搭火箭。我朋友開玩笑說他寧願搭火車上學，因為筷子只能拿來夾麵。不過，推進器被接住的那一刻，全班還是歡呼了起來。

passages.title: 沒有司機的計程車
passages.text: In some American cities, people can now take a taxi with no driver in it. These cars belong to a company called Waymo. You open an app, ask for a {1}, and a car comes to pick you up. Cameras and sensors on the roof help the car see people, bikes, and big {2} on the road. In 2025, Waymo cars gave more than 250,000 paid rides every week, and the number kept growing. My cousin lives in San Francisco, and she {3} in one last summer. At first, she was nervous because the driver's seat was empty. But the car drove slowly and carefully, and it even stopped for a cat. She said it felt as safe as taking a {4}. Still, my grandpa says he will never get into a car without a driver. He would rather take a {5} with a real pilot!

blanks.why: ask for a ride「叫車、要求搭載」，ride 當名詞是「搭乘、一趟車程」。spoon、sock、lemon 都不是打開 app 就會「來接你」的服務。
big trucks on the road「路上的大卡車」。pumpkins（南瓜）、blankets（毯子）、candles（蠟燭）都不會在馬路上行駛。
she rode in one「她搭過一台」，ride 的過去式 rode。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 in one 表示坐車。
as safe as taking a train「跟搭火車一樣安全」。towel（毛巾）、cookie（餅乾）、wallet（錢包）都不能搭乘。
take a plane with a real pilot「搭有真人機長的飛機」。fever（發燒）、cough（咳嗽）、drawer（抽屜）都沒有機長。

gloss: 美國自動駕駛計程車公司
passages.zh: 在美國的一些城市，人們現在可以搭乘沒有司機的計程車。這些車屬於一家叫 Waymo 的公司。你打開 app 叫車，就會有車子來接你。車頂上的攝影機和感應器幫助車子看見路上的行人、腳踏車和大卡車。2025 年，Waymo 的車每週載客超過 25 萬趟付費行程，而且數字還在增加。我表姊住在舊金山，去年夏天她搭過一台。一開始她很緊張，因為駕駛座是空的。但車子開得又慢又小心，甚至還停下來讓一隻貓先過。她說感覺跟搭火車一樣安全。不過，我爺爺說他絕不會坐沒有司機的車，他寧願搭有真人機長的飛機！

passages.title: 掛上風帆的貨船
passages.text: Long ago, every {1} used the wind to sail across the sea. Today, most big cargo ships burn oil, and shipping makes nearly 3% of the world's carbon dioxide. In August 2023, a cargo ship called the Pyxis Ocean tried an old idea in a new way. It left Singapore for Brazil with two giant "WindWings" on its deck. Each sail is about 37.5 meters tall and is made of hard materials, not cloth. The wind pushes the sails, so the ship can use less fuel. Cargo ships carry many things we use every day, from phones to bananas. When they arrive at a port, {2} and {3} carry the goods to stores. My dad works at a port in Kaohsiung, and he loves watching the ships come in. He says he hopes more ships will {4} the wind in the future, so the air will be {5} for everyone.

blanks.why: every ship used the wind to sail「每艘船都靠風航行」。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不會航行。
trucks … carry the goods to stores「卡車把貨物載到商店」。socks（襪子）、candles（蠟燭）、cookies（餅乾）都不能運貨。
trucks and trains「卡車和火車」，都是陸上運輸工具。blankets、lemons、wallets 都不能載貨。
use the wind「利用風力」。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 the wind。
the air will be cleaner「空氣會更乾淨」，clean 的比較級 cleaner。saltier（更鹹）、sourer（更酸）、spicier（更辣）都是味道，不能形容空氣因為少燒油而改善。

passages.zh: 很久以前，每艘船都靠風航行。現在，大部分的大型貨船燒油，航運產生了全世界將近 3% 的二氧化碳。2023 年 8 月，一艘名叫「皮克西斯海洋號」的貨船用新的方式嘗試一個老點子。它從新加坡出發前往巴西，甲板上裝了兩面巨大的「風翼」。每面帆大約 37.5 公尺高，是用堅硬的材料做的，不是布。風推動風帆，船就可以少用一些燃料。貨船運送很多我們每天會用的東西，從手機到香蕉都有。船抵達港口後，卡車和火車再把貨物送到商店。我爸爸在高雄港工作，他很喜歡看船進港。他說希望未來有更多船利用風力，讓每個人的空氣都更乾淨。

passages.title: 高雄輕軌繞成一個圓
passages.text: Kaohsiung has a light rail that looks like a long, quiet {1}. It runs through the city on grass tracks, so parts of the line look like a green carpet. On January 1, 2024, the last section opened, and the line became a full circle. To celebrate, people could {2} it for free until late February. Along one part of the line, big rain trees make a green tunnel over the tracks. The light rail also connects with the MRT, buses, and {3} at several stations. Last weekend, my grandma and I took it around the whole city. We saw the harbor, where a big {4} was coming in, and we stopped for ice cream at the Pier-2 Art Center. Grandma said it was the most relaxing {5} she had taken in years, because she didn't have to drive or look for parking.

blanks.why: looks like a long, quiet train「看起來像一列又長又安靜的火車」。spoon、sock、lemon 都不會在城市裡行駛。
people could ride it for free「大家可以免費搭乘」，could + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不能表示搭乘交通工具。
connects with the MRT, buses, and trains「和捷運、公車、火車轉乘相連」。blankets、candles、cookies 都不是交通工具。
a big ship was coming in「一艘大船正要進港」，harbor 是港口。towel（毛巾）、fever（發燒）、pocket（口袋）都不會進港。
the most relaxing ride「最輕鬆的一趟車程」，ride 當名詞。cough（咳嗽）、headache（頭痛）、receipt（收據）都不能 take 來表示搭乘的經驗。

passages.zh: 高雄的輕軌看起來像一列又長又安靜的火車。它在市區的草皮軌道上行駛，所以有些路段看起來像一條綠色地毯。2024 年 1 月 1 日，最後一段通車，路線終於繞成一個完整的圓。為了慶祝，大家可以免費搭乘到二月底。在其中一段路線上，高大的雨豆樹在軌道上方形成一條綠色隧道。輕軌也在好幾個車站和捷運、公車、火車相連。上週末，我和奶奶搭著它繞了整個城市。我們看到港口有一艘大船正要進港，還在駁二藝術特區停下來吃冰淇淋。奶奶說這是她好幾年來最輕鬆的一趟車程，因為她不用開車，也不用找停車位。

passages.title: 搭飛機耳朵為什麼會痛
passages.text: Have you ever felt pain in your ears when a {1} takes off or lands? This happens because the air pressure in the cabin changes quickly. Behind your eardrum there is a small space full of air. A thin tube connects this space to the back of your nose. When the pressure outside changes, the tube needs to open so the air inside can {2} too. If it doesn't open fast enough, your eardrum is pushed in or out, and it hurts. When the tube finally opens, you hear a small "pop." You can help it open by swallowing, yawning, or chewing gum. That is why some people give babies milk during takeoff and landing. You may feel the same thing when you {3} a fast elevator in a tall building, or when a {4} goes through a long tunnel. My little sister always eats candy on a {5}, and she says it is the best medicine.

blanks.why: when a plane takes off「飛機起飛時」，take off 是起飛。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不會起飛降落。
the air inside can change too「裡面的空氣（壓力）也能改變」。fry、boil、iron 都不能用在空氣壓力上。
ride a fast elevator「搭快速電梯」，ride 也可以接電梯。fry、mop、boil 都不能接 elevator 表示搭乘。
a train goes through a long tunnel「火車穿過長隧道」。sock、lemon、candle 都不會穿過隧道。
eats candy on a plane「在飛機上吃糖」，on a plane 表示搭機時。blanket（毯子）、cough（咳嗽）、drawer（抽屜）都不能 on a… 表示旅途中。

passages.zh: 你有沒有在飛機起飛或降落時覺得耳朵痛？這是因為機艙裡的氣壓變化得很快。在耳膜後面有一個充滿空氣的小空間，一條細細的管子把它連到鼻子後方。外面的氣壓改變時，這條管子需要打開，讓裡面的空氣也跟著調整。如果它打開得不夠快，耳膜就會被往內或往外推，所以會痛。管子終於打開時，你會聽到小小的「啵」一聲。你可以靠吞口水、打哈欠或嚼口香糖幫助它打開，這就是為什麼有些人在起飛降落時給嬰兒喝奶。當你搭高樓的快速電梯，或火車穿過長長的隧道時，也可能有同樣的感覺。我妹妹搭飛機時總是吃糖，她說這是最好的藥。

passages.title: 鋼鐵做的船為什麼不會沉
passages.text: If you drop a small steel coin into water, it sinks. So how can a huge steel {1} float? The answer is its shape. A ship is not a solid block of steel. It is wide and mostly empty inside, so it pushes away a lot of water. The water pushes back up on the ship. About 2,200 years ago, the Greek thinker Archimedes {2} this idea: if an object pushes away water that weighs as much as the object, it floats. You can try it at home. Roll a piece of clay into a ball, and it sinks. Then shape the same clay into a little boat, and it floats! That is also why a cargo ship can carry hundreds of {3} and still stay on top of the water. But if a ship carries too much, it goes too low and may sink. Next time you take a {4} to an island, or {5} a ferry across a river, think of Archimedes!

blanks.why: a huge steel ship「巨大的鋼鐵船」，和前面的硬幣對照。spoon、cookie、sock 都不能用 huge steel 形容並浮在海上。
Archimedes explained this idea「阿基米德解釋了這個概念」。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 idea。
carry hundreds of trucks「載好幾百輛卡車」，大型貨船可以載車輛。coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）、headaches（頭痛）都不是東西，不能被船「載運」。
take a ship to an island「搭船去島上」。lemon、candle、wallet 都不能搭乘。
ride a ferry「搭渡輪」，ride 接交通工具。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 a ferry。

passages.zh: 如果你把一枚小小的鋼製硬幣丟進水裡，它會沉下去。那麼，一艘巨大的鋼鐵船怎麼能浮起來呢？答案是它的形狀。船不是一整塊實心的鋼，它又寬，裡面又大多是空的，所以會推開很多水，而水會把船往上推。大約 2,200 年前，古希臘學者阿基米德解釋了這個概念：如果一個物體推開的水和它自己一樣重，它就會浮起來。你可以在家試試看：把一塊黏土搓成球，它會沉；再把同一塊黏土捏成小船，它就浮起來了！這也是為什麼一艘貨船可以載好幾百輛卡車，還能浮在水面上。但如果船載太多東西，就會吃水太深，可能會沉。下次你搭船去離島，或搭渡輪過河時，想想阿基米德吧！

passages.title: 為什麼會暈車暈船
passages.text: Some people feel sick when they {1} in a car or on a bus. Others feel sick on a {2} or even on a plane. This is called motion sickness. Scientists believe it happens when your senses don't agree. Your inner ear feels the movement, but if you are reading a book or looking at your phone, your eyes tell your brain that you are not moving. The brain gets confused, and you may feel dizzy or want to throw up. There are some easy ways to feel better. Look out the window at the horizon, which stays still. Sit in the front of a car, or sit over the wings on a {3}, where it shakes less. On a {4}, choose a seat that faces forward. Fresh air also helps. Last summer, on our trip to Penghu, I felt terrible until I stopped {5} my phone and looked at the sea instead.

blanks.why: ride in a car「坐車」，ride in + 交通工具。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 in a car。
feel sick on a ship「在船上感到不舒服」，就是暈船。spoon、towel、cookie 上面都不能坐人。
sit over the wings on a plane「坐在飛機機翼上方的位置」，飛機才有 wings。pumpkin、sock、lemon 都沒有機翼。
On a train, choose a seat that faces forward「在火車上選面向前方的座位」。blanket、candle、wallet 都沒有座位。
stopped using my phone「不再用手機」，stop + V-ing 是停止做某事。frying、ironing、boiling 都不能接 my phone。

passages.zh: 有些人坐汽車或公車時會覺得不舒服，有些人則是在船上、甚至搭飛機時會不舒服，這叫做動暈症。科學家認為，這是因為你的感官「意見不合」。你的內耳感覺到在移動，但如果你在看書或看手機，眼睛卻告訴大腦你沒有在動。大腦被搞糊塗了，你就可能覺得頭暈或想吐。有幾個簡單的方法可以讓你好過一點：看窗外靜止不動的地平線；坐在汽車前座，或搭飛機時坐在機翼上方比較不晃的位置；搭火車時選面向前方的座位。呼吸新鮮空氣也有幫助。去年夏天去澎湖的時候，我一直很難受，直到我不再看手機、改看大海才好起來。

passages.title: 萊特兄弟的十二秒
passages.text: On December 17, 1903, near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright lay on the wing of a small {1} and flew it into the air. The flight lasted only 12 seconds and went about 37 meters, a little longer than a basketball court. Still, it was the first time a powered machine carried a person through the air in a controlled flight. Orville and his brother Wilbur did not go to university. They owned a bicycle shop in Ohio, and they used what they learned about bikes to build their flying machine. Before 1903, they tested many gliders and even built their own wind tunnel. That day, they flew four times, and Wilbur's last flight lasted 59 seconds. Today, millions of people {2} in planes every day. Some huge cargo planes can even carry {3} or {4} cars. When I took my first plane trip to Japan, I {5} the two brothers and their 12 seconds.

blanks.why: a small plane「一架小飛機」，可以讓人躺在機翼上飛起來。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都沒有機翼，也不會飛。
people ride in planes「人們搭飛機」，ride in + 交通工具。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 in planes。
carry trucks「載運卡車」，大型貨機可以載車輛。coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）、headaches（頭痛）都不是能被載運的東西。
train cars「火車車廂」，train 在這裡修飾 cars。blanket、candle、cookie 都不能和 cars 組成「車廂」。
I remembered the two brothers「我想起這對兄弟」，remember 是記得、想起。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 the two brothers。

gloss: 小鷹鎮（美國北卡羅來納州）
passages.zh: 1903 年 12 月 17 日，在美國北卡羅來納州的小鷹鎮附近，奧維爾‧萊特趴在一架小飛機的機翼上，讓它飛上天空。這次飛行只有 12 秒，飛了大約 37 公尺，只比一個籃球場長一點。但這是第一次有動力的機器載著人、在可以操控的情況下飛行。奧維爾和哥哥威爾伯沒有讀大學，他們在俄亥俄州開了一家腳踏車店，並把修腳踏車學到的知識用來打造飛行機器。在 1903 年之前，他們測試過很多架滑翔機，甚至自己做了一個風洞。那一天，他們飛了四次，威爾伯最後一次飛了 59 秒。現在，每天有好幾百萬人搭飛機，有些巨大的貨機甚至能載運卡車或火車車廂。我第一次搭飛機去日本時，就想起了這對兄弟和他們的 12 秒。

passages.title: 學翠鳥的新幹線
passages.text: Japan's Shinkansen is a very fast {1}. In the 1990s, engineers had a problem with it. When the train entered a tunnel at high speed, it pushed the air in front of it. When it came out of the tunnel, there was a loud BOOM that people living nearby could hear. An engineer named Eiji Nakatsu was also a bird watcher. He knew that the kingfisher dives from the air into water to catch fish, and it hardly makes a splash. Its long, pointed beak cuts through the water smoothly. So he and his team gave the new 500 Series train a long nose shaped like a kingfisher's beak. It worked! The train became quieter, and it also used less power. This idea of copying nature is called biomimicry. Our science teacher says engineers also study birds to design better {2}, and fish to design faster {3}. Next time I {4} the Taiwan High Speed Rail, I will look at the train's nose and {5} a bird.

blanks.why: a very fast train「很快的火車」，新幹線就是高速列車。spoon、sock、lemon 都不會開進隧道。
design better planes「設計更好的飛機」，研究鳥類有助於設計會飛的東西。pumpkins、towels、candles 都不需要模仿鳥類來設計。
design faster ships「設計更快的船」，研究魚類有助於設計在水中前進的東西。cookies、blankets、wallets 都不會在水中前進。
ride the Taiwan High Speed Rail「搭台灣高鐵」。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 High Speed Rail。
imagine a bird「想像一隻鳥」，imagine 是想像。fry、iron、mop 都不能接 a bird 表示心裡的畫面。

passages.zh: 日本的新幹線是一種非常快的火車。在 1990 年代，工程師遇到一個問題：列車高速開進隧道時，會推擠前方的空氣，出隧道時就會發出「轟」的一聲巨響，連住在附近的人都聽得到。有一位叫仲津英治的工程師，同時也是賞鳥的人。他知道翠鳥從空中衝進水裡抓魚時，幾乎不會濺起水花，因為牠又長又尖的鳥喙能順順地切開水面。於是他和團隊讓新的 500 系列車有一個像翠鳥嘴巴的長鼻子。結果成功了！列車變得更安靜，也更省電。這種模仿大自然的想法叫做仿生學。我們的自然老師說，工程師也會研究鳥類來設計更好的飛機，研究魚類來設計更快的船。下次我搭台灣高鐵時，我要看看列車的車頭，想像一隻鳥。

passages.title: 飛機被閃電打到怎麼辦
passages.text: Many people are afraid of flying in storms. But here is a surprising fact: a passenger {1} is hit by lightning about once a year, and almost nothing happens. Why? The outside of a plane is made mostly of metal or other materials that let electricity pass through easily. When lightning hits, the electricity travels along the outside of the plane and leaves from another point, such as the tail. The people inside are safe. The same idea explains why a car or a {2} with a metal body is a safe place to be during a storm. After a lightning strike, workers check the plane carefully before its next flight. Last year, my uncle was on a flight when lightning hit it. He saw a bright flash and heard a loud bang, but the pilot calmly told everyone not to worry. The plane landed safely, and my uncle took a {3} home. Now he says flying is less scary than the roller coaster he {4} in Japan, which made him {5} much louder.

blanks.why: a passenger plane「客機」。spoon、pumpkin、sock 都不會在暴風雨中飛行。
a car or a truck with a metal body「有金屬車身的汽車或卡車」。towel、candle、lemon 都沒有金屬車身，也不能躲在裡面避雷。
took a train home「搭火車回家」。blanket、cookie、wallet 都不能搭乘。
the roller coaster he rode「他坐過的雲霄飛車」，ride 的過去式 rode，ride 可以接遊樂設施。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 roller coaster。
made him shout「讓他大叫」，make + 人 + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不是坐雲霄飛車時人會發出的反應。

passages.zh: 很多人害怕在暴風雨中搭飛機。但有一個令人驚訝的事實：一架客機大約每年會被閃電打到一次，而且幾乎什麼事都不會發生。為什麼呢？飛機的外殼大多是用金屬或其他容易導電的材料做的。閃電打到時，電會沿著飛機外面流過，再從另一個地方（例如機尾）離開，裡面的人都很安全。同樣的道理也說明了為什麼在暴風雨中，待在金屬車身的汽車或卡車裡是安全的。被閃電打到後，工作人員會在下一次飛行前仔細檢查飛機。去年，我舅舅搭的班機就被閃電打到。他看到一道亮光、聽到一聲巨響，但機長冷靜地告訴大家不用擔心。飛機平安降落，舅舅再搭火車回家。現在他說，搭飛機還沒有他在日本坐的雲霄飛車可怕，那個讓他叫得大聲多了。

passages.title: 戰鬥機護送的十二強冠軍
passages.text: On November 24, 2024, Taiwan beat Japan 4–0 in the final of the WBSC Premier12 at the Tokyo Dome. It was the first time Taiwan had won a major world baseball title like this. The players had {1} hard for years, and nobody expected them to beat Japan, the defending champion. The next evening, the team flew home. When their {2} came close to Taiwan, four F-16 fighter jets flew next to it to welcome the champions home. Thousands of fans waited at Taoyuan Airport, holding signs and shouting the players' names. My uncle was one of them. He took the airport MRT {3} there right after work. He said the station was so crowded that he could hardly get off. When the players walked out, everyone {4} so loudly that he couldn't hear his own voice. Now my uncle keeps a photo of the team as the background of his phone, and he says it was the best {5} home from work he has ever had.

blanks.why: had trained hard「一直努力訓練」，train 當動詞是「訓練、練習」，had + 過去分詞 trained。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能和 hard 搭配表示練球。
their plane came close to Taiwan「他們的飛機接近台灣」。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不會飛，也不能被戰鬥機護航。
the airport MRT train「機場捷運列車」。blanket、candle、lemon 都不能搭乘。
everyone cheered「大家都歡呼」。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能描寫粉絲迎接球員的反應。
the best ride home from work「下班回家最棒的一趟路程」，ride 當名詞。cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）、drawer（抽屜）都不能用來形容回家的路程。

passages.zh: 2024 年 11 月 24 日，台灣在東京巨蛋舉行的世界棒球十二強賽冠軍戰以 4 比 0 打敗日本。這是台灣第一次拿到這樣的重要世界棒球冠軍。球員們多年來一直努力訓練，但沒有人想到他們能打敗衛冕冠軍日本。隔天晚上，球隊搭機回國。他們的飛機接近台灣時，四架 F-16 戰鬥機飛在旁邊，歡迎冠軍回家。好幾千名球迷在桃園機場等待，舉著標語、大喊球員的名字。我舅舅就是其中一個，他一下班就搭機場捷運趕過去。他說車站擠到他差點下不了車。球員走出來時，大家歡呼得好大聲，他連自己的聲音都聽不到。現在舅舅把球隊的照片設成手機桌布，他說那是他下班回家最棒的一趟路。

passages.title: F1 賽車怎麼環遊世界
passages.text: Formula 1 has more than 20 races a year in many countries, from Australia to Brazil. So how do the race cars get there? For races in Europe, teams move their cars and tools by {1}. Each team has a group of big trucks that drive from one track to the next. For races far away, the cars are packed into boxes and sent by cargo {2}. This is the fastest way, but also the most expensive. Things that are heavy but not needed quickly, such as tables, chairs, and kitchen tools, are sent by {3} weeks or even months before the race. Some teams have several sets of these things traveling around the world at the same time. My brother, who loves F1, says the workers who {4} with the trucks and fly with the cars are like a second team. "The drivers race on Sunday," he said, "but the workers {5} against time all year."

blanks.why: move their cars by truck「用卡車運送賽車」，by + 交通工具（不加冠詞）。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能運送賽車。
sent by cargo plane「用貨機運送」，cargo plane 是貨機，後面說這是最快的方法。sock、lemon、candle 都不能運貨。
sent by ship「用船運」，後面說要提早好幾週甚至好幾個月送出，因為海運比較慢。cough、fever、headache 都不能運送東西。
workers who ride with the trucks「跟著卡車一起移動的工作人員」，ride 是乘坐。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 with the trucks。
race against time「和時間賽跑」，race 當動詞是比賽、賽跑。fry、iron、mop 都不能接 against time。

passages.zh: 一級方程式賽車每年在許多國家舉辦二十多場比賽，從澳洲到巴西都有。那麼，賽車是怎麼到那裡的呢？在歐洲比賽時，車隊用卡車運送賽車和工具，每支車隊都有一群大卡車，從一條賽道開到下一條。在很遠的地方比賽時，賽車會被裝進箱子，用貨機送過去，這是最快、但也最貴的方法。重但不急著用的東西，例如桌子、椅子和廚房用具，會在比賽前好幾週甚至好幾個月就用船運送。有些車隊會有好幾套這類東西同時在世界各地移動。我哥哥很愛 F1，他說那些跟著卡車移動、跟著賽車飛來飛去的工作人員就像第二支車隊。他說：「車手星期天比賽，但工作人員一整年都在和時間賽跑。」

passages.title: 搭飛機去奧運的馬
passages.text: At the Paris 2024 Olympics, the horse-riding events took place at the Palace of Versailles. But how did horses from other countries get to France? Many of them flew! For example, the American horses were first driven to an airport in New York. Then they were lifted onto a big cargo {1} and flew about eight hours to Luxembourg. The horses {2} two to a stall, with their own food and water. A vet and two grooms flew with them and checked on them every hour. After the plane landed, the horses took a four-hour trip by {3} to a base camp, and later went on to Versailles. Like human athletes, each horse even had its own passport. I have only {4} a pony once at a farm in Taiwan, but now I know that Olympic horses are very good travelers. Maybe one day I can watch the riders and their horses at the Olympics. I would happily take a {5} all the way to Versailles to see them!

blanks.why: a big cargo plane「一架大貨機」，後面說飛了八小時。spoon、pumpkin、sock 都不能載馬飛行。
The horses rode two to a stall「馬兒兩匹一欄地搭乘」，ride 的過去式 rode，表示乘坐在交通工具上。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能說明馬在飛機上的情形。
by truck「搭卡車」，by + 交通工具，路程四小時。towel、lemon、candle 都不能載馬。
have only ridden a pony once「只騎過一次小馬」，現在完成式 have + 過去分詞，ride 的過去分詞 ridden。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 a pony 表示騎乘。
take a train to Versailles「搭火車到凡爾賽」。cough、fever、drawer 都不能搭乘。

passages.zh: 在 2024 年巴黎奧運，馬術比賽在凡爾賽宮舉行。可是其他國家的馬要怎麼到法國呢？很多都是搭飛機去的！例如美國的馬先被載到紐約的機場，再被吊上一架大貨機，飛大約八小時到盧森堡。馬兒兩匹一欄地搭機，有自己的食物和水，一位獸醫和兩位馬伕跟著一起飛，每小時都去看看牠們。飛機降落後，馬兒再搭四小時的卡車到一個基地營，之後才前往凡爾賽。和人類選手一樣，每匹馬甚至都有自己的護照。我只在台灣的農場騎過一次小馬，但現在我知道奧運的馬都是很厲害的旅行家。也許有一天我能去奧運看騎士和他們的馬，我很樂意一路搭火車到凡爾賽去看牠們！

passages.title: 搭帆船來的奧運聖火
passages.text: Usually, the Olympic flame travels from Greece to the host country by {1}. But for the Paris 2024 Olympics, France chose a slower and more special way. On April 27, 2024, the flame left Athens on the Belem, a three-masted sailing {2} built in 1896. The trip across the Mediterranean Sea took about twelve days. On May 8, the Belem arrived in Marseille, a city that was started by Greek sailors about 2,600 years ago. Hundreds of small boats and {3} sailed next to it as it came into the port. A huge crowd watched from the shore, and a fighter jet team drew the colors of the French flag in the sky. After that, the flame {4} around France for more than two months. My French pen pal Chloé was in Marseille that day. She said it was the most beautiful {5} she had ever seen.

blanks.why: by plane「搭飛機」，by + 交通工具，和後面「更慢、更特別的方式」對比。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能運送聖火。
a sailing ship「一艘帆船」，three-masted 是三根桅杆。sock、lemon、candle 都不能有桅杆、橫渡地中海。
small boats and ships sailed next to it「小船和大船在旁邊航行」。coughs、fevers、headaches 都不能航行。
the flame traveled around France「聖火在法國各地傳遞」，travel 是移動、旅行。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 around France。
the most beautiful ship「最漂亮的船」，指貝倫號。wallet、blanket、cookie 都和進港的帆船無關。

passages.zh: 通常奧運聖火會搭飛機從希臘送到主辦國。但為了 2024 年巴黎奧運，法國選擇了一個比較慢、也更特別的方式。2024 年 4 月 27 日，聖火搭上 1896 年建造的三桅帆船「貝倫號」，從雅典出發，橫越地中海大約花了十二天。5 月 8 日，貝倫號抵達馬賽，這座城市是大約 2,600 年前由希臘水手建立的。進港時，好幾百艘小船和大船在它旁邊航行，岸上擠滿了觀眾，飛行表演隊還在空中畫出法國國旗的顏色。之後，聖火在法國各地傳遞了兩個多月。我的法國筆友克蘿伊那天就在馬賽，她說那是她看過最漂亮的一艘船。

passages.title: 住在郵輪上的奧運衝浪選手
passages.text: The Paris 2024 Olympics had one event that was very far from Paris. The surfing contest was held at Teahupo'o in Tahiti, an island in the South Pacific about 15,000 kilometers away. To get there, the surfers had to take a long {1} trip across the world. Teahupo'o is a small village, and there are not many hotels. So the surfers and their coaches stayed on a cruise {2} called the Aranui 5, which stayed near the coast. It was the first time Olympic athletes ever slept on a ship during the Games. Every morning, they took small boats out to the waves. The waves at Teahupo'o are famous for being big and powerful, and only the best surfers can {3} them safely. In the end, Kauli Vaast from Tahiti won the men's gold medal for France, and Caroline Marks from the United States won the women's gold. My cousin, who surfs in Yilan, watched every {4} on TV. He says he will {5} hard and visit Tahiti one day.

blanks.why: a long plane trip「一趟很長的飛行旅程」，plane 在這裡修飾 trip。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能和 trip 組成交通旅程。
a cruise ship called the Aranui 5「一艘叫阿拉努伊五號的郵輪」。sock、lemon、candle 都不能讓人住在上面。
ride the waves「乘浪、衝浪」，ride 可以接 waves。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 waves。
watched every ride「看了每一次乘浪」，ride 當名詞，指衝浪選手每一次站上浪頭。cough、fever、drawer 都不是比賽中可以觀看的表現。
will train hard「會努力訓練」，train 當動詞，will + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不能和 hard 搭配表示練習。

gloss: 提阿胡普（大溪地衝浪地點）
passages.zh: 2024 年巴黎奧運有一個項目離巴黎非常遠：衝浪比賽在南太平洋的大溪地島上的提阿胡普舉行，距離巴黎大約一萬五千公里。為了到那裡，衝浪選手得搭很久的飛機橫越大半個世界。提阿胡普是個小村莊，旅館不多，所以選手和教練住在一艘停靠在海岸附近、名叫「阿拉努伊五號」的郵輪上。這是奧運選手第一次在比賽期間睡在船上。每天早上，他們搭小船出海去追浪。提阿胡普的浪以又大又猛聞名，只有最厲害的衝浪選手才能安全地駕馭。最後，來自大溪地的考利‧瓦斯特替法國拿下男子金牌，美國的卡洛琳‧馬克斯則拿下女子金牌。我表哥在宜蘭衝浪，他在電視上看了每一次乘浪。他說他會努力訓練，有一天要去大溪地。

passages.title: 塞爾提克的鴨子船遊行
passages.text: In June 2024, the Boston Celtics won their 18th NBA championship, more than any other team in history. On June 21, the city held a parade to celebrate. But the players did not {1} in normal cars or buses. They rode on "duck boats." A duck boat looks like a mix of a {2} and a boat. It has wheels, so it can drive on the road, and it can also float on water like a small {3}. The idea came from vehicles that were used in World War II. Today, tourists in Boston take duck boat tours, and the city's sports teams use them for championship parades. Huge crowds filled the streets that day. Many fans came by {4} from nearby towns. My cousin, who studies in Boston, took photos of Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown waving from the boats. She said she {5} she could jump on one and ride along.

blanks.why: did not ride in normal cars「沒有坐一般的車」，did not + 原形動詞 ride。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 in cars 表示乘坐。
a mix of a truck and a boat「卡車和船的混合體」，後面說它有輪子可以在路上開。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都沒有輪子。
float on water like a small ship「像小船一樣浮在水上」。cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）、headache（頭痛）都不是東西，不會浮在水上。
came by train from nearby towns「從附近城鎮搭火車來」，by + 交通工具。cough、fever、drawer 都不能搭乘。
she wished she could…「她真希望自己能…」，wish 後面接 could 表示不太可能實現的願望。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接子句。

passages.zh: 2024 年 6 月，波士頓塞爾提克隊拿下隊史第 18 座 NBA 總冠軍，比史上任何一支球隊都多。6 月 21 日，城市舉辦遊行來慶祝，但球員們沒有坐一般的汽車或巴士，而是坐在「鴨子船」上。鴨子船看起來像卡車和船的混合體：它有輪子，可以在馬路上開，也能像小船一樣浮在水上。這個點子來自第二次世界大戰時使用的車輛。現在，波士頓的觀光客會搭鴨子船遊覽，城市的運動隊伍拿冠軍時也會用它來遊行。那天街上擠滿了人潮，很多球迷從附近城鎮搭火車過來。我表姊在波士頓讀書，她拍到了塔圖姆和布朗在船上揮手的照片。她說她真希望自己能跳上船，一起坐著遊行。

passages.title: 第一位美國女太空人莎莉‧萊德
passages.text: On June 18, 1983, Sally Ride became the first American woman to go to space. She flew on the space shuttle Challenger, a spaceship that took off like a rocket and landed like a {1}. She was 32 years old, and she was also the youngest American astronaut to go to space at that time. During the trip, she used the shuttle's robot arm to put a satellite into space. In 1984, she went to space for a second time. After she left NASA, she started a company called Sally Ride Science to {2} girls to study science and math. When she died in 2012, people learned that she had shared her life with her partner, Tam O'Shaughnessy, for 27 years. That made her the first known LGBT+ astronaut. Our class read about her in English class. My classmate Jenny said she used to think space was only for men, but now she wants to {3} a rocket one day. "A rocket is just a very fast {4} to the sky," she joked. Our teacher smiled and said, "Then keep studying, and you will get your {5}."

blanks.why: landed like a plane「像飛機一樣降落」，太空梭降落時會在跑道上滑行。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不會降落。
encourage girls to study…「鼓勵女孩讀…」，encourage + 人 + to V。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 girls to study。
ride a rocket「搭火箭」，ride 接交通工具。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 a rocket。
a very fast train to the sky「通往天空的超快火車」，比喻火箭也是交通工具。blanket、candle、lemon 都不能載人。
get your ticket「拿到你的車票」，接著前面把火箭比喻成火車。cough、fever、drawer 都不能「拿到」來搭車。

gloss: 美國國家航空暨太空總署
passages.zh: 1983 年 6 月 18 日，莎莉‧萊德成為第一位上太空的美國女性。她搭乘「挑戰者號」太空梭，這種太空船起飛時像火箭，降落時像飛機。她當時 32 歲，也是那時最年輕上太空的美國太空人。在旅程中，她用太空梭的機械手臂把一顆人造衛星放進太空。1984 年，她第二次上太空。離開美國太空總署後，她成立了「莎莉‧萊德科學」公司，鼓勵女孩學習科學和數學。她在 2012 年過世時，大家才知道她和伴侶譚‧歐修尼西一起生活了 27 年，這讓她成為第一位已知的 LGBT+ 太空人。我們在英文課讀到她的故事。我同學珍妮說她以前以為太空只屬於男生，但現在她想有一天搭火箭上太空。「火箭只是一列開往天空、超快的火車嘛，」她開玩笑說。老師笑著說：「那就繼續用功，你會拿到你的車票。」

passages.title: 羅莎‧帕克斯的公車座位
passages.text: On December 1, 1955, in Montgomery, Alabama, a Black woman named Rosa Parks got on a bus after work. At that time, the law in many parts of the American South said that Black people had to give their seats to white passengers. When the driver told her to stand up, Rosa Parks said no. She was arrested. Her quiet action started the Montgomery Bus Boycott. For 381 days, many Black people in the city refused to {1} the buses. They walked, shared cars, or rode in taxis instead, even in the rain. In 1956, the U.S. Supreme Court said that keeping people apart on buses was against the law. Today, Rosa Parks is remembered as a hero. Her bus is now in a museum, and visitors can sit in it. When I {2} the MRT or take a {3} in Taiwan, I can sit in any open seat. I never thought about it before, but now I know that some people {4} for this kind of fairness. Whether you are on a bus, a {5}, or a train, everyone should be treated the same.

blanks.why: refused to ride the buses「拒絕搭公車」，refuse to + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 the buses。
ride the MRT「搭捷運」。fry、boil、mop 都不能接 the MRT。
take a train「搭火車」。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能搭乘。
some people fought for…「有些人為…奮鬥」，fight 的過去式 fought，fight for 是為某事爭取。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 for 表示爭取。
on a bus, a plane, or a train「在公車、飛機或火車上」，三個都是交通工具。cough、fever、drawer 都不是人搭乘的地方。

passages.zh: 1955 年 12 月 1 日，在阿拉巴馬州的蒙哥馬利，一位名叫羅莎‧帕克斯的黑人女性下班後搭上公車。當時美國南方很多地方的法律規定，黑人必須把座位讓給白人乘客。司機要她站起來時，羅莎‧帕克斯拒絕了，她因此被逮捕。她安靜的行動引發了「蒙哥馬利公車抵制運動」。整整 381 天，城裡許多黑人拒絕搭公車，他們改成走路、共乘或搭計程車，連下雨天也一樣。1956 年，美國最高法院判定在公車上把人分開是違法的。現在，羅莎‧帕克斯被大家當成英雄來紀念。她搭的那輛公車現在放在博物館裡，參觀者可以坐進去。在台灣，我搭捷運或火車時，可以坐任何一個空位。我以前從沒想過這件事，但現在我知道，有些人曾經為這樣的公平奮鬥過。不管是在公車、飛機還是火車上，每個人都應該被平等對待。

passages.title: 飛越大西洋的愛蜜莉亞
passages.text: On May 20, 1932, Amelia Earhart took off from Newfoundland, Canada, in a small red {1}. She wanted to become the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic Ocean. Five years earlier, Charles Lindbergh had made the first solo flight across the Atlantic. During her trip, she flew through strong winds, ice, and darkness, and she had problems with her plane. After about 15 hours, she landed in a farmer's field in Northern Ireland. A surprised farm worker asked her if she had come far, and she told him she had flown from America. At that time, most people crossed the ocean by {2}, and the trip took about a week. Earhart showed that women could be great pilots, too. Today, my aunt is a pilot for a Taiwanese airline. She says that when she was a girl, she read about Earhart and decided to {3} a pilot. Before every flight, she still {4} the weather carefully, just as Earhart did. And when she is not flying, she likes to {5} her bike along the river.

blanks.why: a small red plane「一架紅色小飛機」，後面說她飛越大西洋。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不會飛。
crossed the ocean by ship「搭船橫渡海洋」，by + 交通工具，和搭飛機比較。sock、lemon、candle 都不能載人過海。
decided to become a pilot「決定要成為飛行員」，become 後接名詞。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 a pilot 表示成為。
she still checks the weather「她還是會檢查天氣」，主詞 she 用第三人稱單數 checks。fries、irons、boils 都不能接 the weather。
ride her bike「騎她的腳踏車」。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 her bike。

gloss: 愛蜜莉亞‧艾爾哈特（美國女飛行員）
passages.zh: 1932 年 5 月 20 日，愛蜜莉亞‧艾爾哈特駕著一架紅色小飛機，從加拿大紐芬蘭起飛。她想成為第一位獨自飛越大西洋的女性。五年前，查爾斯‧林白完成了第一次單人飛越大西洋。旅程中，她飛過強風、結冰和黑夜，飛機也出了問題。大約 15 小時後，她降落在北愛爾蘭一位農夫的田裡。一位驚訝的農場工人問她是不是從很遠的地方來，她告訴他自己是從美國飛過來的。當時大部分人是搭船橫渡海洋，要花大約一個星期。艾爾哈特證明女性也能成為很棒的飛行員。現在，我阿姨是台灣一家航空公司的機師。她說她小時候讀到艾爾哈特的故事，就決定要成為飛行員。每次飛行前，她還是會像艾爾哈特一樣仔細檢查天氣。不飛的時候，她喜歡沿著河邊騎腳踏車。

passages.title: 為了飛行去學法文的貝西
passages.text: Bessie Coleman was born in Texas in 1892. When she was young, she worked hard picking cotton and washing clothes. Later, she moved to Chicago and heard stories about pilots who flew in World War I. She dreamed of flying a {1} too. But no flight school in the United States would teach her, because she was a Black woman. Bessie did not give up. She learned French, saved money, and took a {2} across the ocean to France. There, she studied at a flight school, and in 1921 she became the first African American woman to get an international pilot's license. Back in America, she performed in air shows, doing loops and other tricks in the sky. She also {3} to perform at places that did not let Black people in. Today, many young pilots remember her courage. When I take a {4} and {5} a woman pilot's voice, I think of Bessie Coleman, who had to travel so far just to learn to fly.

blanks.why: flying a plane「駕駛飛機」。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能駕駛。
took a ship across the ocean「搭船橫渡海洋」。sock、lemon、candle 都不能載人過海。
refused to perform「拒絕表演」，refuse to + 原形動詞。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 to perform。
take a plane「搭飛機」。cough、fever、drawer 都不能搭乘。
hear a woman pilot's voice「聽到女機長的聲音」。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 voice。

gloss: 貝西‧柯爾曼（美國女飛行員）
passages.zh: 貝西‧柯爾曼 1892 年出生於德州。她年輕時辛苦地採棉花、幫人洗衣服。後來她搬到芝加哥，聽到第一次世界大戰中飛行員的故事，也夢想著自己能開飛機。可是美國沒有一所飛行學校願意教她，因為她是黑人女性。貝西沒有放棄。她學了法文、存錢，搭船橫越大海到法國，在那裡的飛行學校學習。1921 年，她成為第一位取得國際飛行執照的非裔美國女性。回到美國後，她在飛行表演中演出，在空中翻圈、做各種特技。她也拒絕在不讓黑人入場的地方表演。現在，許多年輕的飛行員都記得她的勇氣。當我搭飛機聽到女機長的廣播聲音時，我就會想到貝西‧柯爾曼，她為了學飛行，必須走那麼遠的路。

passages.title: BTS 的〈Airplane pt.2〉
passages.text: In 2018, BTS released a song called "Airplane pt.2" on their album Love Yourself: Tear. The song has a Latin-pop sound, and it looks back on the group's journey. When the members were young, they only dreamed of success. Later, they began to fly around the world on {1} to perform for fans in many countries. The song came after "Airplane," a track from J-Hope's solo mixtape. In November 2018, BTS also released a Japanese version as a single. My cousin, a big ARMY, says this song reminds her of a real trip. Last year, she took a {2} to Seoul for the first time. From the airport, she {3} the airport railroad into the city and listened to "Airplane pt.2" the whole way. Then she took a fast {4} to Busan, where Jimin and Jungkook grew up. She said it felt like she was {5} the boys' journey, one stop at a time.

blanks.why: fly around the world on planes「搭飛機飛遍世界」。spoons、pumpkins、towels 都不能搭乘飛行。
took a plane to Seoul「搭飛機去首爾」。sock、lemon、candle 都不能搭乘。
rode the airport railroad「搭機場鐵路」，ride 的過去式 rode。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 railroad。
a fast train to Busan「開往釜山的快速火車」。cough、fever、drawer 都不能開往某地。
following the boys' journey「跟著團員們的旅程走」，follow 是跟隨。frying、ironing、boiling 都不能接 journey。

gloss: 防彈少年團的粉絲名稱
passages.zh: 2018 年，防彈少年團在專輯《Love Yourself: Tear》中推出一首叫〈Airplane pt.2〉的歌。這首歌帶有拉丁流行的風格，回顧了團體一路走來的旅程：團員們年少時只能夢想成功，後來開始搭著飛機飛遍世界，為許多國家的粉絲表演。這首歌延續了 J-Hope 個人混音帶中的〈Airplane〉。2018 年 11 月，防彈少年團也推出了日文版單曲。我表姊是忠實的 ARMY，她說這首歌讓她想起一次真實的旅行。去年她第一次搭飛機去首爾，從機場搭機場鐵路進市區，一路上都在聽〈Airplane pt.2〉。接著她搭快速火車到智旻和柾國長大的釜山。她說感覺就像一站一站地跟著團員們的旅程走。

passages.title: 智旻和柾國的旅行節目
passages.text: In August 2024, a travel show called Are You Sure?! started on Disney+. It follows two members of BTS, Jimin and Jungkook, on trips they took in 2023. They traveled to New York State in the United States, Jeju Island in South Korea, and Sapporo in Japan. To get to these places, they took long {1} flights. On the trips, they went camping, cooked their own food, swam, and went canoeing on a lake. They also went on road trips. Jeju is an island, so many visitors get there by plane or by {2}. My friend Amy watched every episode. Her favorite part was when the two friends did simple things together, like eating and talking for hours. After watching the show, Amy wants to {3} a bike around Jeju with her best friend. She has already looked up how to {4} her bike there, but her mom says it is easier to rent one on the island. Maybe they will also take a {5} around Japan one day, just like Jimin and Jungkook.

blanks.why: long plane flights「長途飛行」，plane 修飾 flights。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能和 flights 組成搭機旅程。
get there by plane or by ship「搭飛機或搭船到那裡」，濟州島是島嶼。sock、lemon、candle 都不能載人過海。
ride a bike around Jeju「騎腳踏車環繞濟州島」。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 a bike。
how to ship her bike there「怎麼把腳踏車運過去」，ship 當動詞是「運送」。cough、fever、drawer 都是名詞，不能當動詞接 her bike。
take a train around Japan「搭火車遊日本」。blanket、cookie、wallet 都不能搭乘。

passages.zh: 2024 年 8 月，一個叫《Are You Sure?!》的旅遊節目在 Disney+ 上線，記錄防彈少年團的兩位成員智旻和柾國在 2023 年的旅行。他們去了美國紐約州、南韓濟州島和日本札幌。為了到這些地方，他們搭了很久的飛機。旅途中，他們露營、自己煮飯、游泳，還在湖上划獨木舟。他們也開車公路旅行。濟州是一座島，所以很多遊客是搭飛機或搭船過去。我朋友艾美每一集都看了，她最喜歡兩個好朋友一起做簡單小事的片段，例如一起吃飯、聊好幾個小時。看完節目後，艾美想和最好的朋友一起騎腳踏車環濟州島。她已經查過要怎麼把腳踏車運過去，但她媽媽說在島上租一台比較簡單。也許有一天，她們也會像智旻和柾國一樣，搭火車遊日本。

passages.title: 為 BTS 加開的列車
passages.text: On October 15, 2022, BTS held a free concert at the Busan Asiad Main Stadium. The concert was held to support Busan's hope to host the World Expo in 2030. Fans came from all over South Korea and from other countries. To help so many people get to the city, more {1} were added. On the day of the concert, there were extra KTX high-speed trains between Seoul and Busan. More flights between Busan and Japan were also added, so Japanese fans could take a {2} there more easily. Inside the city, the subway and buses ran more often. My cousin was one of the fans. She took a KTX {3} from Seoul in the morning. The ride took about two and a half hours. She said everyone on the train was wearing purple, and some fans were {4} BTS songs quietly. After the concert, she waited a long time for the subway, but she didn't mind. "It was the happiest {5} home of my life," she said.

blanks.why: more trains were added「加開了更多火車班次」。spoons、pumpkins、towels 都不是交通班次。
take a plane there「搭飛機去那裡」，前面說增加了航班。sock、lemon、candle 都不能搭乘。
took a KTX train「搭 KTX 列車」。cough、fever、drawer 都不能搭乘。
fans were singing BTS songs「粉絲在唱 BTS 的歌」，過去進行式 were + V-ing。frying、ironing、boiling 都不能接 songs。
the happiest ride home「最開心的一趟回家路程」，ride 當名詞。blanket、cookie、wallet 都不能用來形容回家的路程。

passages.zh: 2022 年 10 月 15 日，BTS 在釜山亞運主體育場舉辦了一場免費演唱會，目的是支持釜山爭取主辦 2030 年世界博覽會。粉絲們從南韓各地和其他國家趕來。為了幫助這麼多人到達這座城市，相關單位加開了火車班次：演唱會當天，首爾和釜山之間增加了 KTX 高鐵列車；釜山和日本之間的航班也增加了，讓日本粉絲更容易搭飛機過去。在市區裡，地鐵和公車也提高了班次。我表姊就是其中一位粉絲。她早上從首爾搭 KTX 列車出發，車程大約兩個半小時。她說車上每個人都穿紫色，有些粉絲還小聲地唱著 BTS 的歌。演唱會結束後，她等地鐵等了很久，但她一點都不在意。「這是我這輩子最開心的一趟回家路，」她說。

passages.title: 騎著看不見的馬的〈江南 Style〉
passages.text: In July 2012, the Korean singer PSY released the song "Gangnam Style." Its music video became a huge hit around the world. The most famous part was the dance. PSY moved his legs and arms as if he were {1} an invisible horse. People everywhere copied it, from students in schools to players on sports teams. On December 21, 2012, it became the first video on YouTube to reach one billion views. At that time, no other video had ever had so many. My parents still remember dancing it at their office parties. Last month, our class did the "horse {2}" dance at the school sports day, and the younger students laughed so hard. On the {3} home, my little sister kept practicing the moves in her seat. An old man next to us smiled and said he danced it at his grandson's wedding. I think Gangnam Style is like a {4} that never lands, because it keeps flying around the world. Even people who don't speak Korean can {5} the invisible horse with PSY!

blanks.why: as if he were riding an invisible horse「好像在騎一匹看不見的馬」，as if 後面用假設語氣 were + V-ing。frying、ironing、boiling 都不能接 horse 表示騎乘。
the "horse ride" dance「騎馬舞」，ride 當名詞，horse ride 是騎馬。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能和 horse 組成舞蹈名稱。
On the train home「在回家的火車上」，後面說她在座位上練舞。sock、lemon、candle 都沒有座位。
like a plane that never lands「像一架永遠不降落的飛機」，比喻這首歌一直在全世界「飛來飛去」。cough、fever、drawer 都不會降落、飛行。
can ride the invisible horse「可以一起騎那匹看不見的馬」，can + 原形動詞，指跳騎馬舞。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 horse。

passages.zh: 2012 年 7 月，韓國歌手 PSY 推出歌曲〈江南 Style〉，音樂錄影帶在全世界爆紅。最有名的就是那段舞：PSY 擺動雙腿和手臂，好像在騎一匹看不見的馬。世界各地的人都跟著模仿，從學校裡的學生到運動隊伍的球員都有。2012 年 12 月 21 日，它成為 YouTube 上第一支觀看次數達到十億的影片，當時沒有任何影片有過這麼多觀看次數。我爸媽到現在還記得在公司尾牙跳這支舞。上個月，我們班在運動會上跳「騎馬舞」，學弟妹們笑得東倒西歪。在回家的火車上，我妹妹一直坐在位子上練習動作。旁邊一位老先生笑著說，他在孫子的婚禮上也跳過。我覺得〈江南 Style〉就像一架永遠不降落的飛機，一直在全世界飛來飛去。就算不會說韓語的人，也能跟著 PSY 一起騎那匹看不見的馬！

passages.title: 教練說要好好「訓練」
passages.text: Last week, our basketball coach said to the team, "We have a big game on Saturday, so we need to {1} every day this week." My little brother Max is only six. He heard this when he came to watch our practice. The next day, he showed up at the gym with his toy {2} and put it on the court. "I'm ready to train too!" he said proudly. Everyone stopped and looked at him. Then our coach laughed and explained that "train" has two meanings. It can be something you {3} to another city, and it can also mean "to practice hard." Max thought about it for a second. Then he said, "Okay, then my train will practice too!" He pushed it around the court while we ran. Now every time we practice, the coach asks, "Is everybody here? Is the {4} here?" And after we {5} the game on Saturday, Max said his train helped us win.

blanks.why: need to train every day「每天都需要訓練」，train 當動詞，need to + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不是球隊比賽前要做的事。
his toy train「他的玩具火車」。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能加上 toy 變成這個笑話的關鍵，而且後面說它有兩個意思，指的是 train。
something you ride to another city「你搭去另一個城市的東西」，ride 是搭乘。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 to another city。
Is the train here?「火車到了嗎？」，教練在開 Max 的玩具火車的玩笑。cough、fever、drawer 都和這個笑話無關。
we won the game「我們贏了比賽」，win 的過去式 won。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 the game。

passages.zh: 上週，我們的籃球教練對球隊說：「我們星期六有一場重要的比賽，所以這週每天都要訓練。」我弟弟麥克斯才六歲，他來看我們練球時聽到了這句話。隔天，他帶著他的玩具火車出現在體育館，把它放在球場上。「我也準備好要 train 了！」他很驕傲地說。大家都停下來看著他。接著教練笑了，解釋說 train 有兩個意思：它可以是你搭去另一個城市的火車，也可以表示「努力練習」。麥克斯想了一秒鐘，然後說：「好啊，那我的火車也要練習！」我們跑步的時候，他就推著火車在球場上繞。現在每次練球，教練都會問：「大家都到了嗎？火車到了嗎？」星期六我們贏了比賽之後，麥克斯說是他的火車幫我們贏的。

passages.title: 世界上最大的船
passages.text: On the first day of our school trip, our English teacher gave us a riddle on the bus. "What is the biggest {1} in the world?" she asked. Kevin answered right away, "The Icon of the Seas!" Lisa said, "No, it's a big oil ship!" My friend Tom said it must be a spaceship, because space is the biggest place. The teacher shook her head and smiled. "The biggest ship in the world is friendship," she said. Everyone groaned, but we all laughed. On that trip, we took a {2} to Hualien, rode bikes along the coast, and took a {3} out to see dolphins. On the boat, Tom felt sick, so Kevin gave him his seat by the window. Lisa shared her snacks with everyone. On the {4} home, the teacher said, "See? Friendship really is the biggest ship. It can {5} all of you!"

blanks.why: the biggest ship in the world「世界上最大的船」，這是謎題的關鍵，答案是 friendship（友誼）。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能接到後面的答案。
took a train to Hualien「搭火車去花蓮」。sock、lemon、candle 都不能搭乘。
took a ship out to see dolphins「搭船出海看海豚」。cough、fever、drawer 都不能出海。
On the ride home「在回家的路上」，ride 當名詞，指一趟車程。blanket、cookie、wallet 都不能用 on the… home 表示路程。
It can carry all of you「它可以載著你們所有人」，carry 是載運，延續「船」的比喻。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 all of you 表示載人。

passages.zh: 校外教學的第一天，英文老師在遊覽車上給我們出了一個謎語：「世界上最大的船是什麼？」凱文馬上回答：「海洋標誌號！」莉莎說：「不對，是大油輪！」我朋友湯姆說一定是太空船，因為太空是最大的地方。老師搖搖頭笑著說：「世界上最大的船是友誼（friendship）。」大家都哀嚎了一聲，但還是笑了出來。那趟旅行，我們搭火車去花蓮，沿著海岸騎腳踏車，還搭船出海看海豚。在船上，湯姆暈船了，凱文就把靠窗的位子讓給他；莉莎把零食分給大家。在回家的路上，老師說：「看吧？友誼真的是最大的船，它可以載著你們每一個人！」

passages.title: 開卡車的舅舅
passages.text: My uncle drives a big {1} for a company that sells fruit. Every night at three o'clock, he leaves Taichung with boxes of bananas and pineapples, and he arrives at the markets in Taipei before the sun comes up. He says the highway is very quiet at night, and he can see the lights of the cities far away. Last summer, he let me {2} with him for one trip. I sat high up in the front seat, and I could see over all the cars. He showed me how he checks the tires and the lights before he leaves. On the way, we stopped to eat at a rest area. It was full of other truck drivers, and many of them knew my uncle. "Being a truck driver is like being the captain of a {3}," he told me. "Many people are waiting for what you bring." After that night, I never {4} about my early school bus again. Next summer, I want to go with him again, but this time I will take a nap first, and maybe take the {5} home in the morning.

blanks.why: drives a big truck「開一輛大卡車」，後面說他載著一箱箱水果送貨。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能開。
let me ride with him「讓我跟他一起坐車」，let + 人 + 原形動詞。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 with him 表示同行。
the captain of a ship「船長」，比喻卡車司機要負責把貨物平安送到。sock、lemon、candle 都沒有船長。
never complained about…「再也不抱怨…」，complain about 是抱怨某事。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 about。
take the train home「搭火車回家」。cough、fever、drawer 都不能搭乘。

passages.zh: 我舅舅為一家賣水果的公司開大卡車。每天晚上三點，他載著一箱箱香蕉和鳳梨從台中出發，在太陽升起之前抵達台北的市場。他說晚上的高速公路很安靜，還能看到遠方城市的燈光。去年夏天，他讓我跟著跑一趟。我坐在高高的前座，可以看到所有車子的上方。出發前，他示範怎麼檢查輪胎和車燈。途中，我們在休息站停下來吃東西，那裡擠滿了其他卡車司機，很多人都認識我舅舅。「當卡車司機就像當船長一樣，」他對我說，「很多人在等你送來的東西。」那晚之後，我再也沒抱怨過要很早搭校車。明年暑假我還想跟他去，不過這次我會先睡個午覺，早上也許再搭火車回家。

passages.title: 畢業旅行去龜山島
passages.text: For our graduation trip, our class went to Yilan. On the first morning, we took a small {1} from Wushi Harbor to see Guishan Island, which looks like a turtle in the sea. Before we got on, our teacher gave us medicine for seasickness, but the sea was calm, so most of us felt fine. On the way, we saw a group of dolphins jumping next to the boat. Everyone ran to one side to take photos, and the captain had to ask us to {2} back to our seats. In the afternoon, we {3} bikes along the river, and in the evening, we had a barbecue at the hotel. On the last day, we took the {4} back to Taipei. I sat next to my best friend and looked out the window at the green rice fields. We didn't talk much because we were tired, but we were both a little sad. This was our last trip together before we go to different high schools. Maybe someday we will take a {5} to another country together.

blanks.why: took a small ship「搭一艘小船」，從港口出發去看島。spoon、pumpkin、towel 都不能載人出海。
ask us to move back to our seats「要我們回到座位上」，ask + 人 + to V，move 是移動。fry、boil、iron 都不能接 back to our seats。
we rode bikes「我們騎腳踏車」，ride 的過去式 rode。fried、ironed、boiled 都不能接 bikes。
took the train back to Taipei「搭火車回台北」，後面說從車窗看出去。sock、lemon、candle 都沒有車窗。
take a plane to another country「搭飛機去另一個國家」。cough、fever、drawer 都不能搭乘。

passages.zh: 我們班的畢業旅行去了宜蘭。第一天早上，我們從烏石港搭小船去看龜山島，它看起來就像海上的一隻烏龜。上船前，老師發給我們暈船藥，不過海很平靜，大部分的人都沒事。途中，我們看到一群海豚在船邊跳躍。大家都跑到同一邊拍照，船長只好請我們回到座位上。下午我們沿著河邊騎腳踏車，晚上在飯店烤肉。最後一天，我們搭火車回台北。我坐在最好的朋友旁邊，看著窗外綠油油的稻田。我們沒有聊太多，因為都很累，但兩個人心裡都有點難過。這是我們上不同高中之前的最後一次旅行。也許有一天，我們會一起搭飛機去別的國家。
